When you change the retrospective date o.root_cause_full: When you change the retrospective date on CG0435 during the new business term, you see an additional premium of $25. This happens because the system applies a factor based on the number of years prior to the current term. For example, moving the date back to 2016 from 2024 applies a factor of 8 (2024–2016). Since this is a mid-term endorsement, the premium is prorated for the remaining days, which is why the charge is $25 (it could be higher if applied for the full term). On renewal terms, no additional premium is charged, which is correct. As per the code and business requirements, the extra premium applies only on the new business term, not on subsequent renewals.

The wording displayed on FAS is determin.root_cause_full: The wording displayed on FAS is determined by the Additional GL Premium calculation, which currently drives whether the text shows “Additional Premium Due” or “Return Premium.” The logic checks if Additional GL Premium > 0, and if true, displays “Additional Premium Due”; otherwise, it shows “Return Premium.” In this case: Additional GL Premium = GL Premium (11,380) – [Prior Premium Written (10,147) – Change (-1,125)] Calculation: 11,380 – (10,147 – (-1,125)) = 108 Since 108 > 0, the system displayed “Additional Premium Due.” However, the requirement states: Populate “Additional Premium Due” only if Earned Premium – Previously Written Premium results in a positive balance. If negative, display “Return Premium.”
